what_worked: Mica's onboarding call and creative drops are the only thing on this account that has ever consistently earned thanks. The 6/29 Google Meet was booked and run inside nine days of kickoff, and every inspo drop gets a warm reply — 'Thank you🫶🏼🫶🏼' (2026-07-02), 'Thank you! Xxx' (2026-09-15). When we give her something she responds immediately; she is unattended, not disengaged.

Doing the reconciliation work ourselves and then explaining it visibly relieved her. Stephski on 2026-07-13: 'Ah okay, had to dick a bit but found your name in the system, we’re all good here!' and 'there was a fee deducted so the total didnt match thats why it was difficult to find' — she replied 'Oh thank god, and oh I see!'. That is the one time we closed a money loop out loud, and it is the behaviour that has since disappeared.

The pre-invoice heads-up is the single cheapest lever we have and it works every time we use it. 'Hi love! Just letting you know your invoice will be sent tomorrow, so it would be great if you could initiate a OF withdrawl today so the funds hit your account in time!' (2026-09-14) produced payment in two days from a client who was in Yosemite with no phone signal — no chasing required. Paired with Stephski's unprompted apology on 2026-09-16 ('I am so sorry for the back and forth, just want to make sure you have everything you need to make it smooth from here on out ❤️'), it shows the relationship register is right; only the follow-through is missing.
top_fix: Give this account one named owner who posts a single written status message every week — money, platform, deliverables — and enforce one hard rule alongside it: no new invoice goes out while a previous cycle is unconfirmed. Mila had six ALTR staff and no owner, so her suspended-Instagram question (94 days), her promo links (79 days), her 48 uploaded videos (39 days) and four unreconciled payment cycles each died in a different person's lane while every individual person stayed polite and fast. One accountable weekly written status would have caught all of them, and blocking the fifth stacked invoice would have forced the reconciliation that is now the biggest single risk on the account.
